raw_response:
I farm 6 mu in our village — 5 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, and 1 mu in cotton on the south side near the well. I am 72 now, and my wife and I work it alone. Our son is in Shijiazhuang working construction. I have been doing this for 50 years. I finished middle school back in the day, so I can read the fertilizer bags and do the cost sums myself, but most of what I know I learned from my father and from watching which neighbors get good yields.

For the winter wheat on those 5 mu: I will plant the same improved Jimai variety I used last year, about 15 kg of seed per mu. I never skimp on base fertilizer. I will spread one 50-kg bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu before sowing — that is what I have always done, and that is what Lao Wang next door does. Then at green-up I will top-dress with 20 kg of urea per mu, and at the jointing stage another 15 kg of urea per mu. I know that is a lot of nitrogen, about 25 kg per mu in total, but two years ago I tried to save 30 yuan per mu by cutting the second urea dressing, and the wheat turned yellow. I only got 380 kg per mu instead of 450 kg. Losing 70 kg of wheat over a few jin of fertilizer is stupid. I will irrigate four times: once right after sowing to get uniform emergence, once before winter freeze so the wheat does not dry out, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. The well is right there, so water is not the problem — diesel for the pump is. I will spray herbicide once after sowing, and one more spray if I see aphids in April. I will rotary till before planting.

For the summer maize on the same 5 mu: As soon as the wheat is harvested in early June, I plant hybrid corn. I buy Jinhai 5 hybrid seed from the dealer in town — 2 kg per mu. I put down one 50-kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then at the big trumpet stage I spread 30 kg of urea per mu. That comes to about 22 kg of nitrogen per mu. I do not till for corn — I plant straight into the wheat stubble. There is no time to plough, and at my age I need to save labor. I will irrigate three times: at sowing if the soil is dry, at big trumpet, and at grain filling. Two pesticide applications are enough for corn, usually one for armyworm and one if there is rust.

For the cotton on 1 mu: I keep this mu in cotton because my wife can help pick it in autumn, and the cotton income pays for our winter heating coal. I plant an improved cotton seed, not the old traditional kind. Cotton needs more potassium than grain crops, so I put one 50-kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu plus an extra 20 kg of potassium fertilizer per mu. That gives about 18 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 10 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate three times — at planting, at flowering, and at boll stage. Cotton needs more pesticide than grain; I will spray four times, mainly for bollworm and aphids. I will rotary till before sowing.

I expect 450 kg per mu of wheat, 550 kg per mu of corn, and 260 kg per mu of seed cotton. Fertilizer prices went up again this year, but I would rather spend the money than risk a bad harvest. At my age, I do not try new tricks. I do what worked last year.
